scope.description: Three probes on freshly elected three-voter clusters, each stepping one MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2 into a real state machine with any panic recovered: a malformed payload directly into the leader, the same malformed payload into follower 2 (whose forwarded message is then stepped into the leader), and a well-formed payload directly into the leader as the control.
assumptions: The cluster is built with newNetwork and elected by nt.send(MsgHup), so the leader has a committed entry in its term and the follower knows its leader.
The malformed payload is the byte sequence {0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff}, which the library's protobuf decoding rejects.
Proposals are delivered as pb.Message{Type: MsgProp, Entries: [{Type: EntryConfChangeV2, Data: payload}]}, which is the shape a caller or a forwarding follower produces.
The follower's relayed message is stepped into the leader by the harness, which is the same message the transport would deliver.
Panics are recovered by the harness only; in production the same panic escapes (*raft).Step and aborts the caller's raft loop.
excluded: The transport, admission control and any authentication between peers
Snapshots, membership changes, restarts and joint configurations
Any state-machine effect of the proposal, since the malformed payload never reaches the log

basis.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). assuranceCluster-equivalent setup: three real raft instances with newTestRaft(1|2|3, 10, 1, newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) wired with newNetwork and elected by nt.send(MsgHup); the harness asserts node 1 is StateLeader, advances its applied index to its committed index and clears the queues. For each probe it emits conf_proposal_setup with probe_id, scenario, via_follower, data_len, leader, term, leader state, committed and applied; it then steps the proposal with assuranceStepRecover, which recovers any panic and reports the verbatim value plus the messages the node produced. For the malformed-direct probe the proposal is stepped into the leader; for the malformed-via-follower probe it is stepped into follower 2 (whose single forwarded MsgProp to node 1 is recorded and then stepped into the leader, with the leader's own panic recovered); for the valid control a marshalled ConfChangeV2 adding node 4 is stepped into the leader. Each probe emits conf_proposal_outcome with probe_id, scenario, via_follower, follower_panicked, follower_recovered, follower_messages, forwarded_to, leader_panicked, recovered, last_index_before, last_index_after and leader state. The harness asserts that the forwarding hop neither panics nor changes the number of forwarded messages, so a failure at the relay cannot be mistaken for the leader's outcome.
basis.responsibility: The proposal path owns deciding whether a proposal can be turned into log state and reporting a failure to its caller; a payload it cannot decode must be rejected as a proposal rather than converted into an abort of the node that processes it, and a node that relays a proposal owns at least not to propagate a shape it knows the leader will abort on.

comparisons.description: Stepping a proposal with an undecodable conf-change payload directly into a leader does not abort the node.
Relaying the same malformed proposal through a follower does not let it abort the leader that decodes it.
Control: a well-formed conf change of the same entry type is appended without aborting the leader.
